title: Streamlined usage joins and failover for near-real-time billing attribution
creator: Marco Chen
description: Goal: Replace the existing batch-heavy join-and-aggregation path with a hybrid streaming approach that produces near-real-time per-API-key token attribution while providing deterministic failover and bounded duplication for billing. Motivation: customers are reporting large billing surprise windows (6-12h) that block investigating spikes. We need lower time-to-insight for chargeback and the ability to generate provisional invoices during incidents.
background: Current pipeline composes events from request-ingest, token-meter, and model-runtime-annotations using periodic bulk joins in a Spark job. This creates multi-hour visibility delays and brittle re-processing semantics when late events arrive. The engineering team has prototyped a Flink-based streaming join in a spike (see attachments) but several production hardening gaps remain: idempotent upserts to the write-side store, safe watermarking across cross-account clock skews, and graceful degradation to an eventual-consistent summarizer when state store pressure is high.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant attribution latency reduced to < 15 minutes 95th percentile for steady-state traffic
End-to-end duplicate-attribution bounded and discoverable (at most 1.2x provisional duplicates, with reconciliation metrics)
Automatic fallback path to batch summarizer without data loss during sustained state-store write-failure
Comprehensive e2e tests and a canary run that proves correctness on a 10% traffic slice
Observability: new dashboards showing join-lag, watermark skew, state-store memory pressure, and duplicate-rate per-tenant
implementation_notes: Plan is a two-stage rollout: 1) Implement streaming co-group join in Flink with per-tenant keying and event-time watermarks. Use tombstone markers for model annotations to support out-of-order corrections. 2) Materialize a compact streaming view into a strongly-consistent write store (CockroachDB) using idempotent mutation keys (request_id + attribution_version). 3) Add a lightweight summarizer service that can be triggered on-demand to compute a deterministic delta for reconciliation and charging. Trade-offs: CockroachDB provides strong correctness at the cost of higher write latency and cost; alternative explored: RocksDB-backed changelog plus periodic compaction into column store (cheaper but added complexity for cross-region reads). We chose correctness-first for initial rollout and will revisit a colder path later.

Schema and idempotency contract for attribution records (owner: Marco)
Implement CockroachDB write adapter with retry/backoff and oplog-style mutation keys (owner: Priya Rao)
Integrate job with existing ingestion Kafka topics and define retention/watermarks (owner: Data Infra)
End-to-end test harness that replays historical spikes and asserts no-loss (owner: Test Automation)
Create console dashboards and alerts (owner: Observability)
Canary deployment to 10% of traffic and run for 72h with rollback plan (owner: SRE)
risks_and_mitigations: State-store overload during traffic spikes: mitigation: circuit-breaker to degrade to batch summarizer and backpressure producer with tenant-level throttles
Duplicate attributions from retries: mitigation: strict idempotency keys and a reconciliation job that emits correction deltas and audit logs
Time skew causing missed joins: mitigation: implement max allowed skew config per-tenant and a late-event side buffer with reprocessing window
Cost of strongly-consistent store: mitigation: scope to hot window (7 days) in Cockroach and cold-path compaction to cheaper object store
